steps.title: Gate 1: Classify Timing Relative to S1 and S2
steps.ruleQuestion: When in the cardiac cycle does the murmur occur? Use timing first to eliminate half the differential immediately.

paths.ifFinding: Systolic Ejection (Crescendo-Decrescendo)
paths.why: Diamond-shaped peaking mid-systole requires ventricular pressure to overcome outflow resistance; immediately excludes mid-late click MVP, holosystolic regurgitant/shunt lesions, and diastolic murmurs (AR, MS).

paths.ifFinding: Holosystolic (Pansystolic) OR Late Systolic w/ Click
paths.why: Uniform sound from S1 through S2 means an immediate pressure gradient exists at onset of systole (AV valve incompetence or VSD); mid-systolic click → late systolic murmur isolates MVP.

paths.ifFinding: Diastolic (S2→S1) OR Continuous Across S2
paths.why: Diastolic murmurs are NEVER benign flow murmurs—immediately exclude all systolic outflow and AV regurgitant lesions. Continuous machinery peaking AT S2 isolates PDA.

steps.title: Gate 2: Localize Maximal Auscultation Post & Radiation Vector
steps.ruleQuestion: Where on the chest wall is the murmur loudest, and where does turbulent flow radiate?

paths.ifFinding: 2nd Right ICS (RUSB) → Radiates to Carotids
paths.why: Jet directed up the ascending aorta into carotid arteries confirms fixed valvular Aortic Stenosis and EXCLUDES HOCM (which is loudest at LLSB and does NOT radiate to carotids).

paths.ifFinding: 5th ICS Midclavicular (Apex) → Left Axilla
paths.why: Apical location with axillary radiation isolates the mitral valve and EXCLUDES LLSB lesions (TR and VSD).

paths.ifFinding: Left Lower Sternal Border (LLSB) or Left Infraclavicular
paths.why: LLSB + palpable thrill favors VSD; LLSB + inspiratory augmentation favors TR; left infraclavicular machinery murmur confirms PDA.

steps.title: Gate 3: Apply Venous Return Split (Valsalva/Standing vs. Squatting/Inspiration)
steps.ruleQuestion: What happens to murmur intensity when you shrink LV volume (Valsalva / abrupt standing) vs. increase venous return?

paths.ifFinding: LOUDER with Valsalva or Abrupt Standing (↓ Preload)
paths.why: Shrinking the LV chamber narrows the dynamic LVOT in HOCM and slackens chordae earlier in MVP—DECISIVELY EXCLUDING valvular AS and every fixed stenotic/regurgitant murmur!

paths.ifFinding: LOUDER with Inspiration (Carvallo Sign)
paths.why: Inspiratory negative intrathoracic pressure selectively augments right-heart venous return—EXCLUDING left-sided MR and L→R VSD.

paths.ifFinding: LOUDER with Rapid Squatting / Passive Leg Raise (↑ Preload)
paths.why: Higher forward/regurgitant stroke volume intensifies fixed valve lesions while softening HOCM and delaying the MVP click.

steps.title: Gate 4: Apply Isometric Handgrip (↑ Systemic Vascular Resistance)
steps.ruleQuestion: When arterial afterload increases with sustained handgrip, does backward regurgitation increase or forward ejection drop?

paths.ifFinding: LOUDER with Handgrip
paths.why: Clamping systemic arterioles impedes forward aortic exit, forcing more blood backward across MR/AR or across a VSD into the RV—EXCLUDING AS and HOCM.

paths.ifFinding: SOFTER with Handgrip
paths.why: Higher aortic pressure lowers the LV–aorta gradient in AS and distends the LVOT in HOCM, quieting both outflow murmurs.

paths.ifFinding: Louder Leaning Forward at End-Expiration vs. Left Lateral Decubitus
paths.why: Split diastolic murmurs by posture: sitting forward at end-expiration = AR (early decrescendo); left lateral decubitus with bell + opening snap = MS (late diastolic rumble).

steps.title: Gate 5: Confirm Final Diagnosis via Arterial Pulse, S2 Split & PV Loop
steps.ruleQuestion: Which bedside pulse/S2 signature and chamber adaptation locks the single final answer?

paths.ifFinding: Weak Delayed Carotid (Parvus et Tardus) + Soft/Paradoxical S2
paths.why: Confirms severe valvular AS (<70 yo = bicuspid; >70 yo = calcific trileaflet); HOCM instead has a brisk bifid ("jerky") pulse with normal A2.

paths.ifFinding: Wide Pulse Pressure + Bounding Water-Hammer Pulse
paths.why: Diastolic runoff back into LV (AR) or pulmonary artery (PDA) collapses diastolic BP (<60 mmHg); split AR vs. PDA by early diastolic decrescendo vs. continuous machinery murmur.

paths.ifFinding: Opening Snap + Loud S1 + LA Compression Dysphagia/Hoarseness
paths.why: Shorter S2–OS interval = tighter stenosis (higher LA pressure opens stiff rheumatic valve earlier); chronic MR instead shows holosystolic murmur + S3 gallop.

steps.title: Gate 1: Feel Extremity Temperature & Heart Rate (SVR Split)
steps.ruleQuestion: Are extremities warm/flushed (vasodilated ↓ SVR) or cold/clammy (vasoconstricted ↑ SVR)?

paths.ifFinding: WARM Skin + Wide Pulse Pressure (↓↓ SVR)
paths.why: Pathologic peripheral vasodilation lowers SVR—immediately EXCLUDING hypovolemic, cardiogenic, and obstructive shock (all of which clamp down α₁ arterioles → cold clammy skin).

paths.ifFinding: Warm Dry Skin + BRADYCARDIA Post-Spinal Trauma
paths.why: Severed T1–T4 sympathetic outflow uniquely blocks BOTH α₁ vascular tone AND β₁ cardioacceleration—EXCLUDING septic/hemorrhagic shock (which always cause reflex tachycardia).

paths.ifFinding: COLD Clammy Skin + Tachycardia (↑ SVR, ↓ CO)
paths.why: Low cardiac output triggers baroreceptor norepinephrine surge; proceed immediately to Gate 2 (Neck Veins / CVP) to split empty tank vs. pump/obstructive backup.

steps.title: Gate 2: Inspect Jugular Venous Pressure / Central Venous Pressure (CVP)
steps.ruleQuestion: In a cold, clammy hypotensive patient, are neck veins flat (empty tank) or distended (backed-up right heart)?

paths.ifFinding: FLAT Neck Veins (↓↓ CVP & ↓↓ PCWP)
paths.why: Depleted intravascular volume (hemorrhage, burns, GI losses, dehydration) lowers all cardiac filling pressures—DECISIVELY EXCLUDING cardiogenic and obstructive causes.

paths.ifFinding: DISTENDED Neck Veins (↑↑ CVP / JVD)
paths.why: Venous blood cannot move forward through the heart/pulmonary bed—hypovolemia is EXCLUDED; proceed to Gate 3 (Lung Auscultation & PCWP).

steps.title: Gate 3: Auscultate Lungs & Check Pulmonary Capillary Wedge Pressure (PCWP)
steps.ruleQuestion: Are pulmonary bibasilar crackles + high PCWP (>18 mmHg) present, or are the lungs completely CLEAR?

paths.ifFinding: Bibasilar Crackles + HIGH PCWP (>18 mmHg)
paths.why: High left atrial pressure (PCWP) proves left-sided backup or 4-chamber diastolic compression—EXCLUDING isolated right-sided obstruction (Massive PE / Cor pulmonale have NORMAL/LOW PCWP + clear lungs!).

paths.ifFinding: CLEAR Lungs + Normal/Low PCWP + High CVP
paths.why: Clear lung fields in a patient with JVD + hypotension EXCLUDE primary LV pump failure (cardiogenic pulmonary edema) and point to acute RV outflow block (PE) or pericardial tamponade!

steps.title: Gate 4: Split Tamponade vs. Constrictive Pericarditis vs. Massive PE
steps.ruleQuestion: Check heart sounds, Pulsus Paradoxus, Kussmaul sign, and JVP x/y descents:

paths.ifFinding: Muffled Heart Sounds + Pulsus Paradoxus (>10 mmHg) + Absent y-Descent
paths.why: Fluid-filled pericardial sac equalizes diastolic pressures across all 4 chambers (`RA = RV = LA = PCWP`) and prevents diastolic RV relaxation (absent y-descent)—EXCLUDING constrictive pericarditis.

paths.ifFinding: Kussmaul Sign (↑ JVP on Inspiration) + Pericardial Knock + Steep y-Descent
paths.why: Rigid calcified pericardial shell allows rapid early filling (prominent y-descent) before halting abruptly (knock)—EXCLUDING tamponade.

paths.ifFinding: Loud P2 + Acute Hypoxemia + Recent Surgery/Immobilization/DVT
paths.why: Normal heart sounds (not muffled) + V/Q dead-space hypoxemia + RV strain on echo/CT angiogram locks Saddle PE.

steps.title: Gate 5: Confirm Underlying Trigger on 12-Lead ECG & Bedside Echo
steps.ruleQuestion: What final ECG / Echo hallmark seals the single diagnosis?

paths.ifFinding: Low-Voltage QRS + Electrical Alternans + Swinging Heart on Echo
paths.why: Pathognomonic beat-to-beat QRS amplitude oscillation inside pericardial fluid (post-MI free-wall rupture at days 3–14, malignancy, trauma, uremia).

paths.ifFinding: Contiguous ST-Elevations (V1–V4 LAD) or New Severe Apical Holosystolic Murmur
paths.why: Confirms massive anterior LV infarction (>40% myocardium lost) or post-MI posteromedial papillary muscle rupture.

steps.title: Gate 1: Split Nephritic vs. Nephrotic by 24h Urine Protein & Sediment Casts
steps.ruleQuestion: Does urinalysis show RBC casts + HTN (<3.5 g/d protein) OR frothy >3.5 g/d proteinuria + Maltese-cross fatty casts?

paths.ifFinding: Dysmorphic RBCs + RBC Casts + HTN (<3.5 g/day Protein)
paths.why: RBC casts prove inflammatory GBM rupture (Nephritic)—immediately EXCLUDING pure podocyte nephrotic diseases (MCD, pure FSGS, pure Membranous), which have bland sediment without RBC casts.

paths.ifFinding: >3.5 g/day Proteinuria + Hypoalbuminemia + Fatty Casts (No RBC Casts)
paths.why: Massive podocyte barrier loss without glomerular inflammation isolates the Nephrotic pathway (Note: Lupus Class V & MPGN can present mixed/nephrotic).

steps.title: Gate 2 (Nephritic): Check Serum C3 Complement & Post-Infection Latency
steps.ruleQuestion: Is serum C3 LOW (consumed by immune complexes) or NORMAL, and how many days elapsed since pharyngitis/URI?

paths.ifFinding: LOW Serum C3 (Complement Consumed)
paths.why: Hypocomplementemia IMMEDIATELY EXCLUDES IgA nephropathy, Goodpasture, all ANCA vasculitides, and Alport syndrome (all of which maintain NORMAL C3)!

paths.ifFinding: NORMAL C3 + Cola Urine 1–5 Days After Viral URI ("Synpharyngitic")
paths.why: Concurrent mucosal infection flare + normal C3 locks IgA Nephropathy and EXCLUDES PSGN (which requires a 2–3 week latent period + low C3!).

paths.ifFinding: NORMAL C3 + Hemoptysis / Sinusitis / Deafness
paths.why: Pulmonary-renal syndrome (hemoptysis + RPGN) narrows to Goodpasture vs. ANCA vasculitis; family hx of deafness + ocular lens defect in a boy isolates X-linked Alport (COL4A5).

steps.title: Gate 3: Apply Renal Biopsy Immunofluorescence (Linear vs. Pauci vs. Granular)
steps.ruleQuestion: What staining pattern appears on Immunofluorescence (IF) microscopy?

paths.ifFinding: Smooth LINEAR IgG Along GBM
paths.why: Anti-α3(IV) collagen antibodies bind uniformly along intrinsic GBM—DECISIVELY EXCLUDING GPA/MPA (pauci-immune negative IF) and immune-complex diseases (lumpy granular IF).

paths.ifFinding: PAUCI-IMMUNE (Negative / Minimal IF Staining)
paths.why: Absence of immune deposits in crescentic RPGN rules out Goodpasture & SLE: split ANCA subtypes via c-ANCA/PR3 + sinus/saddle-nose (GPA) vs. p-ANCA/MPO without granulomas (MPA) vs. asthma + eosinophilia (EGPA).

paths.ifFinding: GRANULAR IF ("Starry Sky" / "Full-House" / PLA2R)
paths.why: "Full-house" (IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q) = Lupus nephritis; granular subepithelial IgG/C3 2–3 wks post-GAS = PSGN; granular anti-PLA2R without inflammation = Membranous. Note: MCD & primary FSGS are IF-NEGATIVE!

steps.title: Gate 4 (Nephrotic): Split Normal LM vs. Segmental Sclerosis vs. Thick Capillary Loops
steps.ruleQuestion: In IF-negative nephrotic syndrome, is Light Microscopy completely normal or sclerotic, and does prednisone induce remission?

paths.ifFinding: Completely NORMAL Light Microscopy + Steroid-Responsive Child
paths.why: Normal glomeruli on LM + selective albuminuria responding dramatically to corticosteroids confirms MCD (also linked to Hodgkin lymphoma) and EXCLUDES FSGS & Membranous.

paths.ifFinding: Segmental Sclerosis & Hyalinosis on LM + Steroid-Resistant / HIV / Sickle Cell
paths.why: Segmental capillary collapse & hyalinosis in Black/Hispanic adults, HIV, heroin use, or steroid-refractory children locks FSGS and EXCLUDES MCD.

paths.ifFinding: Diffuse Capillary Wall Thickening ("Wire Loops" vs. "Tram-Tracks" vs. "Spike & Dome")
paths.why: Silver stain spikes around subepithelial deposits = Membranous; mesangial ingrowth splitting GBM into double-contour tram-tracks = MPGN (Hep B/C or C3 nephritic factor).

steps.title: Gate 5: Lock Final Diagnosis on Electron Microscopy (EM)
steps.ruleQuestion: Which exact ultrastructural EM location seals the diagnosis beyond doubt?

paths.ifFinding: Isolated Podocyte Foot Process Effacement (ZERO Dense Deposits)
paths.why: Absence of electron-dense deposits rules out all immune-complex nephropathies; split MCD vs. FSGS via LM (normal vs. segmental sclerosis).

paths.ifFinding: Subepithelial Humps vs. Subepithelial Spike-and-Dome vs. Subendothelial
paths.why: Large discrete subepithelial humps = PSGN; subepithelial deposits encased by GBM spikes = Membranous; subendothelial deposits = Diffuse Proliferative Lupus & MPGN Type I; intramembranous ribbon = Dense Deposit (MPGN II).

paths.ifFinding: Alternating Thinning & Laminated "Basket-Weave" GBM Splitting
paths.why: Defective α5(IV) collagen chains fail to form a stable network—confirming Alport and EXCLUDING benign familial hematuria (uniformly thin GBM without lamellation or deafness).

steps.title: Gate 1: Calculate Serum Anion Gap `Na⁺ − (Cl⁻ + HCO₃⁻)` (Normal = 8–12)
steps.ruleQuestion: In pH <7.35 with low HCO₃⁻, are unmeasured organic/toxic anions present (AG >12) or is Cl⁻ elevated (Normal AG = 8–12)?

paths.ifFinding: HIGH Anion Gap (>12 mEq/L, Normochloremic)
paths.why: Unmeasured organic acids titrate HCO₃⁻ without raising Cl⁻—IMMEDIATELY EXCLUDING diarrhea and all Renal Tubular Acidoses!

paths.ifFinding: NORMAL Anion Gap (8–12 mEq/L, Hyperchloremic)
paths.why: Direct HCO₃⁻ loss or impaired H⁺/NH₄⁺ excretion is compensated by Cl⁻ retention—EXCLUDING MUDPILES organic acidoses.

steps.title: Gate 2 (High AG): Check PaCO₂ (Winter Formula), Ketones, Lactate & Osmolar Gap
steps.ruleQuestion: Is there a concomitant respiratory alkalosis, high osmolar gap (`Measured − Calculated >10`), or ketonuria?

paths.ifFinding: Mixed Respiratory Alkalosis (PaCO₂ LOWER Than Winter Formula) + Tinnitus
paths.why: Aspirin directly stimulates the medullary respiratory center first (early respiratory alkalosis) AND uncouples oxidative phosphorylation (high-AG acidosis)—a classic mixed acid-base signature!

paths.ifFinding: Osmolar Gap >10 mOsm/kg + Visual Blur OR Envelope Oxalate Crystals
paths.why: Parent alcohols raise serum osmolality before alcohol dehydrogenase forms toxic formic acid (Methanol → optic disc hyperemia/blindness) or oxalic acid (Ethylene glycol → calcium oxalate crystals + ATN); treat w/ fomepizole!

paths.ifFinding: Normal Osmolar Gap + β-Hydroxybutyrate OR Tissue Hypoperfusion/Metformin
paths.why: Hyperglycemia + Kussmaul breathing + fruity acetone = DKA; shock/sepsis/bowel ischemia/cyanide/metformin in renal failure = Lactic acidosis.

steps.title: Gate 3 (Normal AG): Use Urine Anion Gap `(U_Na + U_K − U_Cl)` to Split Gut vs. Kidney
steps.ruleQuestion: Is the kidney appropriately excreting NH₄Cl (negative Urine AG) or failing to acidify/excrete NH₄⁺ (positive Urine AG)?

paths.ifFinding: NEGATIVE Urine Anion Gap (Abundant Urinary NH₄⁺Cl⁻)
paths.why: Healthy kidneys respond to GI bicarbonate loss (secretory diarrhea, laxatives, ureterosigmoidostomy) by pumping out NH₄Cl—EXCLUDING distal/hyperkalemic RTA!

paths.ifFinding: POSITIVE Urine Anion Gap (Impaired Renal NH₄⁺ Excretion)
paths.why: Proves intrinsic renal tubular acidification defect—proceed to Gate 4 (Serum Potassium) to separate the 3 RTAs instantly.

steps.title: Gate 4 (RTA Split): Check Serum K⁺ (Hyperkalemia vs. Hypokalemia)
steps.ruleQuestion: Only ONE RTA causes Hyperkalemia—which way is serum K⁺ pointing?

paths.ifFinding: HYPERKALEMIA (K⁺ >5.2 mEq/L)
paths.why: Aldosterone deficiency or resistance (diabetic hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism, ACEi/ARB, spironolactone, TMP-SMX, Addison) impairs principal-cell K⁺ secretion AND NH₃ synthesis—EXCLUDING Types 1 & 2!

paths.ifFinding: HYPOKALEMIA (K⁺ <3.5 mEq/L)
paths.why: High distal Na⁺ delivery stimulates aldosterone-driven K⁺ wasting in both Type 1 and Type 2—proceed to Gate 5 (Urine pH) for the final split.

steps.title: Gate 5: Lock RTA Type 1 vs. Type 2 Using Urine pH (<5.5 vs. >5.5) & Stone/Bone Clues
steps.ruleQuestion: During systemic acidemia, can the collecting duct ever lower urine pH below 5.5?

paths.ifFinding: Urine pH PERSISTENTLY > 5.5 + Calcium Phosphate Kidney Stones
paths.why: Defective α-intercalated apical H⁺-ATPase (Sjögren, SLE, amphotericin B) can NEVER acidify urine; alkaline urine + bone Ca²⁺ buffering precipitates bilateral calcium phosphate nephrocalcinosis!

paths.ifFinding: Urine pH < 5.5 (Once Serum HCO₃⁻ Drops) + Fanconi Glycosuria/Phosphaturia
paths.why: PCT HCO₃⁻ reabsorption threshold is lowered (multiple myeloma light chains, Wilson, cystinosis, tenofovir, acetazolamide), but intact distal α-intercalated cells still acidify urine <5.5 once filtered HCO₃⁻ falls below the new threshold; causes hypophosphatemic rickets/osteomalacia (NO stones!).

steps.title: Gate 1: Compute A-a O₂ Gradient (`PAO₂ − PaO₂`, Normal = 10–15 mmHg)
steps.ruleQuestion: Is alveolar-capillary gas transfer intact (Normal A-a gradient) or impaired (Elevated A-a gradient)?

paths.ifFinding: NORMAL A-a Gradient + Elevated PaCO₂
paths.why: Normal A-a gradient proves the lung parenchyma and vasculature are 100% healthy—IMMEDIATELY EXCLUDING all intrinsic airway, interstitial, vascular, and shunt lung diseases! (High altitude also has normal A-a with LOW PaCO₂).

paths.ifFinding: ELEVATED A-a Gradient (>15–20 mmHg)
paths.why: Widened A-a gradient proves V/Q mismatch, diffusion fibrosis, or right-to-left shunt—pure hypoventilation is EXCLUDED.

steps.title: Gate 2: Administer 100% Supplemental O₂ (V/Q Mismatch vs. True Shunt)
steps.ruleQuestion: Does PaO₂ rise briskly on 100% O₂, or does hypoxemia remain refractory?

paths.ifFinding: PaO₂ CORRECTS on 100% O₂
paths.why: Even poorly ventilated or fibrotic alveoli eventually saturate with 100% O₂—EXCLUDING severe right-to-left shunts.

paths.ifFinding: PaO₂ FAILS TO CORRECT on 100% O₂ (True Shunt, V/Q = 0)
paths.why: Blood perfusing completely fluid/pus-filled alveoli (ARDS, pneumonia) or bypassing lungs entirely (Eisenmenger/TOF/HHT pulmonary AVM) never touches inspired O₂!

steps.title: Gate 3 (Chronic Dyspnea): Check FEV1/FVC, TLC & DLCO
steps.ruleQuestion: Is airflow obstructed (`FEV1/FVC <70%`) or restricted (`↓ TLC`), and is DLCO normal or reduced?

paths.ifFinding: FEV1/FVC < 70% + ↑ TLC / ↑ RV
paths.why: Airflow obstruction excludes restrictive ILD; split Emphysema (↓↓ DLCO from destroyed alveolar walls) vs. Chronic Bronchitis & Asthma (normal/↑ DLCO + >12% albuterol reversibility in asthma!).

paths.ifFinding: FEV1/FVC ≥ 75% + ↓ TLC + ↓↓ DLCO
paths.why: Reduced TLC + low DLCO confirms intrinsic parenchymal thickening (IPF bibasilar honeycombing, pneumoconioses, sarcoidosis) and EXCLUDES chest-wall/neuromuscular restriction (which has NORMAL DLCO!).

steps.title: Gate 4 (Acute Hypoxemia): Split Clear CXR vs. Focal Lobar vs. Diffuse White-Out
steps.ruleQuestion: What does the chest X-ray show, and is PCWP ≤18 mmHg?

paths.ifFinding: Sudden Dyspnea + Tachycardia + CLEAR CXR + Respiratory Alkalosis
paths.why: Acute dead-space vascular occlusion leaves alveoli air-filled (clear CXR) with zero wheezes—confirm via CT pulmonary angiogram.

paths.ifFinding: Diffuse Bilateral Alveolar Infiltrates + PaO₂/FiO₂ ≤300 + PCWP ≤18 mmHg
paths.why: Normal PCWP EXCLUDES cardiogenic pulmonary edema and confirms noncardiogenic alveolar-capillary leak (sepsis, pancreatitis, trauma, aspiration → hyaline membranes & loss of Type II pneumocytes).

steps.title: Gate 5: Physical Exam Percussion & Tactile Fremitus Elimination Check
steps.ruleQuestion: In unilateral dullness or dyspnea, how do fremitus and tracheal shift exclude pleural effusion vs. consolidation vs. atelectasis?

paths.ifFinding: Dullness + INCREASED Tactile Fremitus + Bronchial Breath Sounds
paths.why: Solid fluid/pus-consolidated alveoli conduct vocal vibrations BETTER than air (Lobar Pneumonia, trachea midline)—EXCLUDING pleural effusion & mucus-plug atelectasis (both have DECREASED fremitus; atelectasis pulls trachea IPSILATERAL!).

paths.ifFinding: Bilateral Hilar Adenopathy + Noncaseating Granulomas + ↑ 1,25-(OH)₂D₃
paths.why: Locks Sarcoidosis (vs. UIP/IPF subpleural honeycombing or shipbuilder pleural plaques + ferruginous bodies in Asbestosis).

steps.title: Gate 1: Fractionate Serum Bilirubin & Urine Bilirubin Dipstick
steps.ruleQuestion: Is hyperbilirubinemia predominantly Unconjugated (urine bilirubin NEGATIVE) or Conjugated (dark urine bilirubin POSITIVE)?

paths.ifFinding: Predominantly UNCONJUGATED (Indirect) · Urine Bilirubin (−)
paths.why: Albumin-bound indirect bilirubin cannot filter into urine—IMMEDIATELY EXCLUDING all biliary obstructive and canalicular excretion disorders!

paths.ifFinding: Predominantly CONJUGATED (Direct) · Dark Urine Bilirubin (+)
paths.why: Water-soluble conjugated bilirubin spills into urine—EXCLUDING pure hemolysis and UGT1A1 conjugation defects.

steps.title: Gate 2: Eliminate Hemolysis & Benign Hereditary Rotor/Dubin-Johnson
steps.ruleQuestion: Are CBC/reticulocytes/haptoglobin abnormal, OR are AST, ALT, and ALP completely NORMAL?

paths.ifFinding: Indirect Bilirubin + ↓ Haptoglobin + ↑ LDH + ↑ Reticulocytes
paths.why: Elevated RBC turnover overloads hepatic conjugation; normal Hb/retics/haptoglobin instead isolates UGT1A1 defects: mild fasting/stress jaundice = Gilbert; severe neonatal >20 mg/dL kernicterus = Crigler-Najjar Type I.

paths.ifFinding: Direct (Conjugated) Bilirubin + COMPLETELY NORMAL AST, ALT & ALP
paths.why: Normal ALP and normal transaminases EXCLUDE biliary obstruction and hepatitis! Grossly BLACK liver (MRP2 defect) = Dubin-Johnson; normal liver color (OATP1B1/1B3 defect) = Rotor.

steps.title: Gate 3: Split Hepatocellular Pattern (AST/ALT ↑↑) vs. Cholestatic Pattern (ALP/GGT ↑↑)
steps.ruleQuestion: Do aminotransferases dominate (hepatocyte necrosis) or does Alkaline Phosphatase + GGT dominate (bile duct stasis)?

paths.ifFinding: AST & ALT Predominate (Especially >500–1,000 U/L OR AST:ALT >2:1)
paths.why: AST/ALT >1,000 = acute viral, acetaminophen, or ischemic shock liver. AST:ALT >2:1 (both <300) + Mallory-Denk bodies = Alcoholic hepatitis (B6 depletion lowers ALT!).

paths.ifFinding: ALP & GGT Predominate + Pruritus / Pale Stools
paths.why: Elevated canalicular ALP + GGT confirms biliary obstruction/destruction—proceed to Gate 4 (RUQ Ultrasound Common Bile Duct Diameter).

steps.title: Gate 4 (Cholestatic): Check Extrahepatic Bile Duct Dilation on Imaging
steps.ruleQuestion: Is the Common Bile Duct dilated (extrahepatic mechanical block) or nondilated/beaded?

paths.ifFinding: DILATED Extrahepatic Bile Ducts on RUQ Ultrasound
paths.why: Colicky RUQ pain + fever + jaundice (Charcot triad) = Ascending Cholangitis from gallstone; PAINLESS jaundice + palpable nontender gallbladder (Courvoisier sign) + weight loss + migratory thrombophlebitis = Pancreatic Head Adenocarcinoma!

paths.ifFinding: NONDILATED Extrahepatic Ducts + Middle-Aged Woman + AMA (+)
paths.why: Anti-Mitochondrial Antibody (+) + lymphocytic/granulomatous destruction of microscopic INTRAHEPATIC bile ducts locks PBC and EXCLUDES PSC.

paths.ifFinding: Alternating Intra/Extrahepatic "Beads-on-a-String" + Ulcerative Colitis
paths.why: Concentric "onion-skin" bile duct fibrosis in a man with Ulcerative Colitis (p-ANCA+, AMA−) locks PSC (high cholangiocarcinoma risk!).

steps.title: Gate 5 (Chronic Liver): Lock Inherited Copper vs. Iron vs. α1-AT Overload
steps.ruleQuestion: In unexplained young cirrhosis or family history, what metabolic screen eliminates all other causes?

paths.ifFinding: Age <40 + Low Ceruloplasmin + Kayser-Fleischer Rings + Dysarthria/Tremor
paths.why: ATP7B failure → high urinary free copper + basal ganglia putamen atrophy locks Wilson Disease; Transferrin saturation >45% + Ferritin >1,000 + bronze diabetes + HFE C282Y locks Hereditary Hemochromatosis.

steps.title: Gate 1: Measure Serum Intact PTH (PTH-Mediated vs. PTH-Independent)
steps.ruleQuestion: Is intact PTH elevated/inappropriately normal (driving the high Ca²⁺) or suppressed (<20 pg/mL by negative feedback)?

paths.ifFinding: HIGH or Inappropriately Normal Intact PTH
paths.why: Healthy parathyroid glands suppress PTH whenever Ca²⁺ rises—unsuppressed PTH IMMEDIATELY EXCLUDES malignancy, PTHrP, sarcoidosis, and vitamin D toxicity!

paths.ifFinding: SUPPRESSED Intact PTH (↓↓ PTH)
paths.why: Normal parathyroid negative feedback proves an extraparathyroid source of calcium mobilization—proceed to Gate 3 (Phosphate & PTHrP/Vit D).

steps.title: Gate 2 (High PTH): Check 24-Hour Urinary Calcium & Renal Function
steps.ruleQuestion: Before ever recommending parathyroidectomy, is 24-hour urine calcium high/normal or VERY LOW (<100 mg/day)?

paths.ifFinding: VERY LOW 24h Urine Calcium (<100 mg/d · Ca/Cr Clearance <0.01)
paths.why: Inactivating CaSR mutation in parathyroid + thick ascending limb causes lifelong benign asymptomatic hypercalcemia with avid renal Ca²⁺ retention—EXCLUDES Primary HyperPTH (SURGERY IS CONTRAINDICATED!).

paths.ifFinding: HIGH / Normal Urine Calcium + LOW Phosphate + Normal GFR
paths.why: Filtered Ca²⁺ load exceeds tubular reabsorption → calcium stones + subperiosteal bone resorption (85% solitary adenoma; screen for MEN 1 / 2A if young). Note: longstanding ESRD + HIGH PO₄³⁻ + very high PTH = Tertiary HyperPTH.

steps.title: Gate 3 (Suppressed PTH): Split by Serum Phosphate (LOW PO₄³⁻ vs. HIGH PO₄³⁻)
steps.ruleQuestion: In PTH-suppressed hypercalcemia, is serum phosphate LOW (PTHrP phosphaturia) or HIGH (gut absorption / bone lysis)?

paths.ifFinding: ↓↓ PTH + ↑↑ Ca²⁺ + LOW Serum Phosphate (↓ PO₄³⁻)
paths.why: PTHrP binds PTH1 receptors on bone AND proximal tubules (wasting phosphate just like PTH while NOT cross-reacting on the intact PTH assay!)—classic for Squamous Cell Lung & Renal Cell Carcinoma.

paths.ifFinding: ↓↓ PTH + ↑ Ca²⁺ + HIGH/Normal Serum Phosphate (↑ PO₄³⁻)
paths.why: Vitamin D excess and direct bone destruction release/absorb BOTH calcium AND phosphate simultaneously—EXCLUDING PTHrP.

steps.title: Gate 4: Measure 25-OH Vitamin D vs. 1,25-(OH)₂ Vitamin D (Calcitriol)
steps.ruleQuestion: Are vitamin D metabolites elevated (25-OH vs. 1,25-dihydroxy), or are BOTH suppressed?

paths.ifFinding: Normal 25-OH Vit D + ELEVATED 1,25-(OH)₂D₃ (Calcitriol)
paths.why: Unregulated IFN-γ–activated epithelioid macrophages express 1α-hydroxylase (also seen in Hodgkin/B-cell lymphomas & fungal granulomas); responds rapidly to glucocorticoids!

paths.ifFinding: MARKEDLY ELEVATED 25-OH Vitamin D (>150 ng/mL)
paths.why: Exogenous supplement megadosing raises hepatic storage 25-OH Vitamin D directly.

paths.ifFinding: BOTH 25-OH and 1,25-(OH)₂ Vitamin D LOW / Suppressed
paths.why: Local osteoclast RANKL/IL-6 activation (Multiple Myeloma punched-out lytic lesions + M-spike + anemia + renal failure, or breast cancer metastases) liberates bone Ca²⁺ & PO₄³⁻ while suppressing both PTH and renal 1α-hydroxylase.

steps.title: Gate 5: Final Medication Exclusion Check (Thiazides & Lithium)
steps.ruleQuestion: Before invasive workup in mild hypercalcemia, check the medication list:

paths.ifFinding: Patient Taking Hydrochlorothiazide / Chlorthalidone
paths.why: Thiazides inhibit DCT Na⁺/Cl⁻ cotransporter → enhance basolateral Na⁺/Ca²⁺ exchange → ↓ urinary Ca²⁺ excretion (contrast Loop diuretics like furosemide, which INCREASE urinary Ca²⁺ loss!).

steps.title: Gate 1: Check Serum TSH Alongside Free T4
steps.ruleQuestion: In high Free T4, is TSH suppressed (<0.05) or elevated/inappropriately normal?

paths.ifFinding: HIGH Free T4 + HIGH / Unsuppressed TSH
paths.why: Autonomous pituitary thyrotroph adenoma ignores T4 negative feedback (confirm w/ pituitary MRI; rule out thyroid hormone receptor-β resistance).

paths.ifFinding: HIGH Free T4 + SUPPRESSED TSH (↓↓ TSH)
paths.why: Confirms primary/peripheral thyrotoxicosis—proceed immediately to Gate 2 (Eye/Skin & Neck Palpation) and Gate 3 (RAIU Scan).

steps.title: Gate 2: Inspect Eyes/Shins & Palpate Thyroid Pain vs. Nodules
steps.ruleQuestion: Is there exophthalmos/pretibial myxedema, or an exquisitely tender jaw-radiating thyroid?

paths.ifFinding: Exophthalmos (Proptosis) + Pretibial Myxedema + Diffuse Bruit
paths.why: ONLY TSI autoantibodies stimulate orbital and dermal fibroblast TSH receptors to deposit GAGs—PATHOGNOMONICALLY EXCLUDING every other cause of hyperthyroidism!

paths.ifFinding: EXQUISITELY TENDER Thyroid Post-URI + Jaw Pain + ↑↑ ESR
paths.why: Painful thyroid tenderness immediately EXCLUDES Graves, toxic adenoma, and painless postpartum thyroiditis.

steps.title: Gate 3: Run 24-Hour Radioactive Iodine Uptake (RAIU) Scan
steps.ruleQuestion: Is the gland actively trapping iodine (HIGH RAIU) or leaking preformed hormone / suppressed (LOW RAIU)?

paths.ifFinding: HIGH Diffuse Homogeneous RAIU
paths.why: Global receptor stimulation (TSI in Graves, or massive β-hCG α-subunit cross-reactivity in molar pregnancy).

paths.ifFinding: HIGH Patchy / Focal Hot Nodule(s) w/ Cold Surrounding Tissue
paths.why: Gain-of-function TSHR mutation in autonomous nodule(s) suppresses TSH so surrounding normal follicles go dark.

paths.ifFinding: VERY LOW / Absent Neck RAIU (<5%)
paths.why: Follicular destruction leaks stored colloid OR exogenous T4 suppresses endogenous uptake—Graves & Toxic MNG are 100% EXCLUDED! (Rare pelvic uptake = Struma ovarii).

steps.title: Gate 4 (Low RAIU): Split Thyroiditis vs. Surreptitious T4 Using Serum Thyroglobulin
steps.ruleQuestion: When neck RAIU is near zero, is endogenous colloid leaking into blood (↑ Thyroglobulin) or completely shut off (↓↓ Thyroglobulin)?

paths.ifFinding: LOW RAIU + UNDETECTABLE / Very Low Serum Thyroglobulin + Shrunken Gland
paths.why: Oral levothyroxine pills contain pure T4 with ZERO thyroglobulin, suppressing TSH and starving endogenous follicles—DECISIVELY EXCLUDING all destructive thyroiditides!

paths.ifFinding: LOW RAIU + ELEVATED Serum Thyroglobulin
paths.why: Ruptured follicles spill stored thyroglobulin alongside T4/T3 into the bloodstream.

steps.title: Gate 5: Confirm Autoantibody & Triphasic Course
steps.ruleQuestion: What final serology separates painless lymphocytic thyroiditis from de Quervain?

paths.ifFinding: Nontender Gland + Anti-TPO (+) Within 1 Year of Delivery
paths.why: Autoimmune lymphocytic Hashimoto-variant flare causing transient hyperthyroidism → transient hypothyroidism → euthyroid recovery (vs. painful multinucleated giant-cell granulomas in de Quervain).

funnels.chiefComplaint: Primary Amenorrhea & Disorders of Sex Development

steps.title: Gate 1: Check Secondary Sexual Breast Development (Tanner Staging)
steps.ruleQuestion: Are breasts PRESENT (endogenous estrogen IS being produced) or ABSENT (zero estrogen)?

paths.ifFinding: Breasts PRESENT (Estrogen +)
paths.why: Breast development proves intact ovaries (or peripheral aromatization of high testosterone)—IMMEDIATELY EXCLUDING Turner streak gonads, Kallmann GnRH deficiency, and 17α-hydroxylase block!

paths.ifFinding: Breasts ABSENT (Estrogen −)
paths.why: Absence of breast buds proves estrogen deficiency—anatomical outflow defects and CAIS are EXCLUDED; proceed to Gate 3 (Serum FSH).

steps.title: Gate 2 (Breasts +): Check Pelvic Ultrasound for Uterus & Speculum Outflow
steps.ruleQuestion: In a teen with normal breasts and primary amenorrhea, is a UTERUS present or absent?

paths.ifFinding: Uterus PRESENT + Cyclic Pelvic Pain + Bluish Bulging Perineal Membrane
paths.why: Hematocolpos (trapped menstrual blood) proves functional ovaries AND intact uterus—surgical incision cures!

paths.ifFinding: Uterus ABSENT (Blind Vaginal Pouch) + NORMAL Pubic/Axillary Hair (46,XX)
paths.why: Normal female ovaries & adrenals produce normal female testosterone → intact pubic/axillary hair + normal female testosterone levels—DECISIVELY EXCLUDING 46,XY CAIS! (Check renal ultrasound for unilateral renal agenesis!).

paths.ifFinding: Uterus ABSENT + SPARSE/ABSENT Pubic & Axillary Hair (46,XY)
paths.why: Mutated androgen receptor cannot respond to testosterone/DHT (zero sexual hair), while functional Sertoli AMH regressed the uterus and aromatase converted high male testosterone → estradiol (breasts+); remove cryptorchid testes post-puberty!

steps.title: Gate 3 (Breasts −): Measure Serum FSH (Primary Gonadal vs. Central Hypothalamic)
steps.ruleQuestion: In absent breasts (estrogen −), is FSH SKY-HIGH (primary gonadal failure) or LOW (central GnRH/pituitary failure)?

paths.ifFinding: LOW / Normal FSH & LH + Anosmia OR Low BMI Athlete/Anorexia
paths.why: Failed migration of GnRH neurons + olfactory bulb (KAL1/ANOS1 anosmia = Kallmann) or leptin drop from extreme exercise/stress suppresses pulsatile GnRH—EXCLUDING primary gonadal dysgenesis.

paths.ifFinding: HIGH FSH & LH (Hypergonadotropic Hypogonadism)
paths.why: Pituitary is screaming at non-producing gonads—proceed to Gate 4 (Blood Pressure & Karyotype).

steps.title: Gate 4 (High FSH): Split Turner Syndrome vs. 17α-Hydroxylase Deficiency
steps.ruleQuestion: Check Stature, Blood Pressure, Serum Potassium, and Karyotype:

paths.ifFinding: Short Stature + Webbed Neck + Widely Spaced Nipples + 45,XO
paths.why: Menopause before menarche from ovarian follicle atresia (fibrous streak gonads); screen for bicuspid aortic valve, preductal coarctation & horseshoe kidney.

paths.ifFinding: HYPERTENSION + HYPOKALEMIA + Absent Pubic Hair (46,XX or 46,XY)
paths.why: Blocked conversion of pregnenolone/progesterone to cortisol AND all sex steroids shunts everything into mineralocorticoid 11-DOC (HTN + ↓ K⁺ + ↓ renin) with zero estrogens/androgens!
paths.topicTitle: Adrenal steroids and congenital adrenal hyperplasias

steps.title: Gate 5: Exclude 46,XY 5α-Reductase Deficiency ("Guevedoces")
steps.ruleQuestion: What if a child raised as female with blind vaginal pouch suddenly develops muscle mass, deep voice & phallic growth at age 12?

paths.ifFinding: 46,XY + No Uterus + Normal Testosterone : High Testosterone/DHT Ratio at Puberty
paths.why: Unlike CAIS (androgen receptors dead → develops breasts, never virilizes), 5α-reductase deficiency has WORKING androgen receptors—so the pubertal surge of testicular testosterone virilizes external genitalia and grows muscle without gynecomastia!

steps.title: Gate 1: Stratify Immediately by Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV)
steps.ruleQuestion: Is MCV <80 fL (hemoglobin synthesis defect), 80–100 fL (loss/hemolysis/marrow), or >100 fL (DNA synthesis/membrane)?

paths.ifFinding: MICROCYTIC (MCV < 80 fL)
paths.why: Extra cell divisions waiting for heme/globin ("TAILS")—IMMEDIATELY EXCLUDES B12, folate, aplastic anemia, and pure hemolytic anemias!

paths.ifFinding: NORMOCYTIC (MCV 80–100 fL)
paths.why: Narrows to increased destruction (hemolysis/acute bleed) vs. underproduction (early ACD, CKD ↓ EPO, marrow aplasia)—proceed to Reticulocyte Count.

paths.ifFinding: MACROCYTIC (MCV > 100 fL)
paths.why: Impaired thymidine DNA synthesis or membrane lipid excess—all microcytic causes are 100% EXCLUDED.

steps.title: Gate 2 (Microcytic): Split TAILS Using Ferritin, TIBC & Serum Iron
steps.ruleQuestion: In microcytic anemia, is storage Ferritin depleted, locked in macrophages, or overloaded?

paths.ifFinding: ↓↓ Ferritin + ↑↑ TIBC + ↓ Serum Iron + ↑ RDW
paths.why: Low ferritin is 100% diagnostic of depleted body iron stores (rule out colon cancer in older adults!)—EXCLUDING ACD, thalassemia, and sideroblastic anemia.

paths.ifFinding: ↑ Ferritin + ↓↓ TIBC + ↓ Serum Iron (RA / SLE / Cancer / Chronic Infection)
paths.why: IL-6 → hepcidin degrades ferroportin, trapping iron inside macrophages (↑ ferritin, ↓ TIBC)—EXCLUDING iron deficiency (which ALWAYS raises TIBC!).

paths.ifFinding: NORMAL/↑ Iron & Ferritin → Check RBC Count vs. Ringed Sideroblasts
paths.why: Normal RDW + HIGH RBC count + target cells = Thalassemia (↑ HbA2 >3.5% on electrophoresis = β-thal minor; normal HbA2 = α-thal trait). ↑↑ Serum iron + ringed sideroblasts / basophilic stippling = Sideroblastic (B6/INH/ALAS2) or Lead poisoning!

steps.title: Gate 3 (Macrocytic): Check Hypersegmented PMNs & Methylmalonic Acid (MMA)
steps.ruleQuestion: Are neutrophils ≥6-lobed (megaloblastic), and does MMA rise alongside homocysteine?

paths.ifFinding: NO Hypersegmented Neutrophils
paths.why: Absence of megaloblastic nuclear-cytoplasmic dyssynchrony EXCLUDES B12 and Folate deficiency (points to alcohol toxicity, chronic liver disease, hypothyroidism, or brisk reticulocytosis).

paths.ifFinding: Hypersegmented PMNs + ↑ Homocysteine + NORMAL MMA
paths.why: Normal MMA proves methylmalonyl-CoA mutase (B12-dependent) is working normally—confirming Folate deficiency (stores depleted in 3–4 months; zero neurologic damage).

paths.ifFinding: Hypersegmented PMNs + ↑ Homocysteine + ↑↑ MMA + Dorsal Column Loss
paths.why: Elevated MMA is unique to Cobalamin deficiency (pernicious anti-IF Ab, terminal ileal Crohn/resection, strict vegan >3 yrs, D. latum).

steps.title: Gate 4 (Normocytic): Split Reticulocyte Index (<2% vs. >2%) & Direct Coombs Test
steps.ruleQuestion: Is the bone marrow responding briskly (Reticulocytes >2% → Hemolysis) or failing (<2% → Hypoproliferative)?

paths.ifFinding: LOW Reticulocytes (<2%) + Pancytopenia + Hypocellular Fatty Marrow
paths.why: Low reticulocytes EXCLUDE hemolysis! Isolated normocytic anemia in renal failure = ↓ EPO; pancytopenia + hypocellular marrow = Parvovirus B19 (pure RBC aplasia), Fanconi anemia, chloramphenicol/benzene/carbamazepine.

paths.ifFinding: HIGH Reticulocytes (>2%) + ↓ Haptoglobin + ↑ Indirect Bilirubin + Spherocytes
paths.why: Split spherocytes immediately with Direct Coombs (DAT): Coombs (+) = Warm IgG (SLE/CLL/methyldopa) or Cold IgM AIHA; Coombs (−) + ↑ MCHC + family hx + splenomegaly = Hereditary Spherocytosis (spectrin/ankyrin)!

steps.title: Gate 5 (Coombs-Negative Hemolysis): Lock Final Diagnosis by Peripheral Smear & Flow
steps.ruleQuestion: In Coombs-negative normocytic hemolysis, what smear/flow signature locks the exact mechanism?

paths.ifFinding: Bite Cells + Heinz Bodies After Sulfa / Primaquine / Fava / Infection
paths.why: Locks X-linked G6PD deficiency; Sickled drepanocytes + Howell-Jolly bodies = HbSS; Dark morning hemoglobinuria + hepatic vein thrombosis + absent CD55/CD59 on flow cytometry = PNH!

startingPool: Vitamin K Def. / Warfarin / Liver Failure

steps.title: Gate 1: Check Platelet Count First
steps.ruleQuestion: Are platelets LOW (<100,000/mm³) or NORMAL (150,000–400,000/mm³)?

paths.ifFinding: THROMBOCYTOPENIA (↓ Platelets → Petechiae & Mucosal Epistaxis)
paths.why: Low platelet number immediately EXCLUDES pure hemophilia and vWD (Note: Bernard-Soulier has mild thrombocytopenia with GIANT platelets).

paths.ifFinding: NORMAL Platelet Count
keeps: Vitamin K Def. / Warfarin / Liver Failure
paths.why: Normal platelet count EXCLUDES ITP, TTP, HUS, and fulminant DIC—proceed to Gate 3 (PT & aPTT).

steps.title: Gate 2 (Low Platelets): Split ITP vs. TTP/HUS vs. DIC Using PT/PTT & Smear Schistocytes
steps.ruleQuestion: In thrombocytopenia, are schistocytes (helmet cells) present, and are PT/aPTT normal or prolonged?

paths.ifFinding: ZERO Schistocytes + NORMAL PT/aPTT + ↑ Bone Marrow Megakaryocytes
paths.why: Isolated splenic macrophage Fc phagocytosis of anti-GpIIb/IIIa–coated platelets (post-viral child or SLE/HIV adult) leaves RBCs & clotting cascade untouched—EXCLUDING MAHA (TTP/HUS) and DIC!

paths.ifFinding: SCHISTOCYTES (+) + NORMAL PT & NORMAL aPTT
paths.why: Normal PT, normal aPTT & normal fibrinogen DECISIVELY EXCLUDE DIC! Split TTP (adult neuro changes + fever, ADAMTS13 deficiency → plasmapheresis!) vs. Typical HUS (child post-bloody diarrhea EHEC O157:H7 Shiga-like toxin!).

paths.ifFinding: SCHISTOCYTES (+) + PROLONGED PT & aPTT + ↑↑ D-Dimer + ↓↓ Fibrinogen
paths.why: Simultaneous consumption of platelets AND coagulation factors with secondary fibrinolysis confirms DIC (sepsis, obstetrics, trauma, t(15;17) APL) and EXCLUDES TTP/HUS.

steps.title: Gate 3 (Normal Platelets): Read PT & aPTT Combination
steps.ruleQuestion: Are PT and aPTT normal, is aPTT isolated prolonged, or are BOTH PT & aPTT prolonged?

paths.ifFinding: Isolated ↑ aPTT + NORMAL PT + NORMAL Bleeding Time (Deep Hemarthrosis)
excludes: Vitamin K Def. / Warfarin / Liver Failure
paths.why: Normal bleeding time + deep joint/muscle hematomas in a male isolates intrinsic X-linked Factor VIII (Hemophilia A) or IX (Hemophilia B)—EXCLUDING vWD (which prolongs bleeding time & causes mucosal bleeding!).

paths.ifFinding: ↑ Bleeding Time + ↑/Normal aPTT + NORMAL PT (Mucosal/Menorrhagia)
excludes: Vitamin K Def. / Warfarin / Liver Failure
paths.why: vWF bridges GpIb adhesion (↑ BT) AND carries Factor VIII (↑ aPTT)—confirm via ristocetin cofactor assay; responds to DDAVP!

paths.ifFinding: ↑ PT (First) → ↑ BOTH PT & aPTT + Normal Platelets
keeps: Vitamin K Def. / Warfarin / Liver Failure
paths.why: Factor VII has the shortest half-life (4–6h), raising PT first before II, IX, X raise aPTT (neonatal lack of gut flora Vit K, warfarin, malabsorption, or cirrhosis—note Factor VIII is made in endothelium so VIII stays normal/high in liver failure vs. low in DIC!).

steps.title: Gate 4: Run 1:1 Plasma Mixing Study & Ristocetin Platelet Agglutination
steps.ruleQuestion: Does 1:1 normal plasma correct the prolonged aPTT, and does ristocetin clump platelets?

paths.ifFinding: aPTT CORRECTS on Mixing Study → Factor Deficiency (VIII, IX, XI)
paths.why: 50% factor activity normalizes aPTT. Warning: If aPTT FAILS to correct AND patient has DVT/recurrent miscarriages rather than bleeding → Lupus Anticoagulant (antiphospholipid syndrome)!

paths.ifFinding: Normal PT/aPTT + ↑↑ Bleeding Time → Split by Ristocetin
paths.why: Abnormal ristocetin that DOES NOT correct w/ normal plasma + GIANT platelets = Bernard-Soulier (GpIb defect). NORMAL ristocetin + zero ADP/collagen aggregation = Glanzmann thrombasthenia (GpIIb/IIIa defect). (Also exclude Uremic platelet dysfunction!).

steps.title: Gate 5: Verify Inheritance & Treatment Contraindication Check
steps.ruleQuestion: Final clinical safety exclusion before choosing therapy:

paths.ifFinding: Autosomal Dominant Male/Female Mucosal Bleeder vs. X-Linked Boy w/ Hemarthrosis
paths.why: vWD = AD → DDAVP; Hemophilia A = XLR Factor VIII concentrate (mild A also responds to DDAVP; Hemophilia B requires Factor IX, NOT DDAVP!).

steps.title: Gate 1: Check Deep Tendon Reflexes, Tone & Babinski Sign
steps.ruleQuestion: Are reflexes brisk with Babinski (+) (UMN), absent with atrophy (LMN/neuropathy), or NORMAL with pure fatigability (NMJ/Muscle)?

paths.ifFinding: HYPERREFLEXIA + Spasticity + Upgoing Babinski (UMN)
paths.why: UMN signs prove corticospinal tract damage above the anterior horn—IMMEDIATELY EXCLUDING peripheral neuropathy (GBS), NMJ (MG), and primary myopathies!

paths.ifFinding: AREFLEXIA / Hyporeflexia + Ascending Flaccid Weakness
paths.why: Lost Achilles/patellar reflexes post-GI/URI infection isolates peripheral Schwann-cell demyelination (GBS); presynaptic Ca²⁺ channel LEMS also depresses reflexes (which return briefly after exercise!).

paths.ifFinding: NORMAL Reflexes + ZERO Sensory Loss (NMJ or Proximal Muscle)
paths.why: Intact sensation + intact reflexes narrows directly to postsynaptic NMJ (Myasthenia) vs. inflammatory myopathy!

steps.title: Gate 2 (UMN): Split Cortex vs. Internal Capsule vs. Brainstem vs. Cord
steps.ruleQuestion: Check face vs. arm vs. leg pattern, aphasia/neglect, cranial nerve crossing, and sensory level:

paths.ifFinding: Face + Arm > Leg WITH Aphasia (Left) or Hemineglect (Right) | OR Leg > Arm
paths.why: Cortical signs (aphasia, neglect, gaze preference toward lesion) ONLY occur in cerebral cortex strokes (MCA = face/arm; ACA = leg)—EXCLUDING lacunar internal capsule and brainstem!

paths.ifFinding: PURE Motor Unilateral Face + Arm + Leg Equally (NO Sensory Loss, NO Aphasia)
paths.why: Packed corticospinal/corticobulbar fibers in posterior limb of internal capsule (hypertensive lenticulostriate lipohyalinosis) hit face, arm & leg equally without cortical or crossed cranial signs.

paths.ifFinding: CROSSED Signs (Ipsilateral Cranial Nerve + Contralateral Body Tract)
paths.why: Ipsilateral CN III (midbrain Weber), CN VI/VII (pons), or CN IX/X/XII/Horner (medulla) paired with contralateral body deficits PATHOGNOMONICALLY localizes to the Brainstem!

steps.title: Gate 3: Split Spinal Cord Sensory Level vs. Pure Motor ALS
steps.ruleQuestion: When limbs show UMN signs sparing the face, is there a sensory level/bowel-bladder loss or pure UMN+LMN?

paths.ifFinding: BOTH UMN (Babinski/Hyperreflexia) AND LMN (Tongue/Hand Fasciculations) + ZERO Sensory Loss
paths.why: Combined UMN + LMN signs across bulbar/cervical/lumbar regions with 100% intact sensation & normal MRI EXCLUDES cervical cord compression/syringomyelia and locks ALS!

steps.title: Gate 4 (NMJ / Muscle): Test Repetitive Use, Ocular Ptosis & Serum CK
steps.ruleQuestion: Does weakness involve eyelids/extraocular muscles, worsen or improve with use, or spike serum Creatine Kinase (CK)?

paths.ifFinding: Ptosis & Diplopia WORSENING at End of Day / Sustained Upward Gaze · Normal CK
paths.why: Postsynaptic anti-AChR depletion causes classic ocular fatigability (check chest CT for Thymoma!)—EXCLUDING myositis (spares eyes, high CK) and LEMS (improves with use).

paths.ifFinding: Proximal Leg Weakness + Dry Mouth IMPROVING w/ Repeated Exercise in Smoker
paths.why: Repeated depolarization builds up presynaptic Ca²⁺ against paraneoplastic SCLC anti-P/Q Ca²⁺ channel antibodies, transiently restoring ACh release (minimal response to AChE inhibitors!).

paths.ifFinding: Symmetric Proximal Shoulder/Hip Weakness (Spares Eyes!) + Markedly ↑↑ CK
paths.why: Elevated CK + anti-Jo-1 proves muscle fiber destruction; add heliotrope eyelid rash + Gottron knuckle papules → Dermatomyositis (screen for occult malignancy!). Note: Normal CK + >50 yo shoulder stiffness + ↑↑ ESR = Polymyalgia rheumatica!

steps.title: Gate 5: Confirm Guillain-Barré CSF Albuminocytologic Dissociation
steps.ruleQuestion: What lumbar puncture CSF profile locks GBS and excludes infectious poliomyelitis/transverse myelitis?

paths.ifFinding: CSF ↑↑ Protein with NORMAL WBC Count (<5 cells/mm³)
paths.why: Inflamed nerve roots leak protein without CSF pleocytosis (post-Campylobacter jejuni molecular mimicry); monitor vital capacity (FVC) for diaphragm failure and treat w/ IVIG or plasmapheresis (glucocorticoids are INEFFECTIVE!).

steps.title: Gate 1 (Acute Hot Joint): Aspirate Synovial Fluid WBC Count First
steps.ruleQuestion: In an acutely swollen, warm joint, what is the synovial WBC/mm³ count? Never miss a joint-destroying infection!

paths.ifFinding: Purulent Synovial WBC > 50,000/mm³ (>90% PMNs)
paths.why: Septic arthritis until proven otherwise! S. aureus #1 overall; young sexually active patient w/ migratory polyarthralgia + tenosynovitis + pustules = Disseminated N. gonorrhoeae (ceftriaxone).

paths.ifFinding: Inflammatory Synovial WBC 2,000 – 50,000/mm³
paths.why: Inflammatory synovitis EXCLUDES non-inflammatory osteoarthritis (<2,000 WBC/mm³)—proceed immediately to Polarized Light Microscopy.

paths.ifFinding: Non-Inflammatory Clear Viscous Fluid (<2,000 WBC/mm³)
paths.why: Mechanical articular cartilage wear-and-tear (worse at end of day, crepitus, asymmetric knees/hips + DIP Heberden & PIP Bouchard osteophytes).

steps.title: Gate 2: Inspect Polarized Light Microscopy for Crystals
steps.ruleQuestion: Are needle-shaped or rhomboid crystals present, and what color are they parallel to the compensator?

paths.ifFinding: NEEDLE-Shaped · NEGATIVELY Birefringent (Yellow Parallel)
paths.why: Monosodium urate (1st MTP podagra, thiazide/alcohol/meat/Lesch-Nyhan/tumor lysis)—DECISIVELY EXCLUDES Pseudogout.

paths.ifFinding: RHOMBOID-Shaped · POSITIVELY Birefringent (Blue Parallel) + Chondrocalcinosis
paths.why: Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate in knee/wrist cartilage; always screen for Hemochromatosis, Hyperparathyroidism & Hypothyroidism!

steps.title: Gate 3 (Crystal-Negative Chronic Arthritis): Check DIP Involvement & Morning Stiffness
steps.ruleQuestion: Are the Distal Interphalangeal (DIP) joints spared or involved, and is the spine/sacroiliac joint fused?

paths.ifFinding: Symmetric MCP + PIP + Wrist Synovitis · SPARES DIP · Morning Stiffness >60 min
paths.why: Symmetric MCP/PIP distribution sparing DIP EXCLUDES Osteoarthritis and Psoriatic arthritis!

paths.ifFinding: Asymmetric Oligoarthritis / DIP "Sausage Digits" OR Sacroiliitis (RF Negative!)
paths.why: Seronegative HLA-B27 spondyloarthropathies: Psoriatic = dactylitis + nail pitting + DIP "pencil-in-cup" X-ray; Ankylosing spondylitis = young man back stiffness improving w/ exercise + bamboo spine + anterior uveitis; Reactive = post-Chlamydia/Shigella/Campylobacter urethritis + conjunctivitis + arthritis.

steps.title: Gate 4 (Symmetric MCP/PIP): Split Erosive RA vs. Non-Erosive Jaccoud SLE
steps.ruleQuestion: Do hand X-rays show marginal bone erosions + pannus, or non-erosive migratory polyarthritis with malar rash?

paths.ifFinding: Marginal Bone Erosions + Ulnar Deviation + Anti-CCP (+) / RF (+)
paths.why: HLA-DR4 synovial pannus destroys cartilage/bone (anti-citrullinated peptide >95% specific!)—EXCLUDING SLE.

paths.ifFinding: NON-EROSIVE Migratory Arthritis + ANA / Anti-dsDNA / Anti-Sm (+) + Cytopenias
paths.why: SLE causes symmetric hand pain WITHOUT radiographic bone erosions (reducible Jaccoud arthropathy).

steps.title: Gate 5: Mandatory Pre-Treatment Safety Exclusion
steps.ruleQuestion: Before starting methotrexate or anti-TNF-α (infliximab/adalimumab/etanercept) in RA/Psoriatic/AS:

paths.ifFinding: Screen Latent TB (IGRA / PPD) & Hepatitis B Before Anti-TNF; Pregnancy Before MTX
paths.why: TNF-α maintains macrophage granuloma walls—blocking TNF-α reactivates disseminated miliary TB!

steps.title: Gate 1: Triage Acute Febrile Desquamating Emergencies vs. Chronic Autoimmune/Viral
steps.ruleQuestion: Did acute diffuse skin sloughing + high fever erupt rapidly in a newborn/child or days after lamotrigine/sulfa/allopurinol?

paths.ifFinding: Acute Febrile Diffuse Sheets of Skin Sloughing (Nikolsky +)
paths.why: Fulminant acute febrile desquamation isolates drug-induced SJS/TEN vs. toxin-mediated SSSS—proceed immediately to Gate 2 (Oral/Ocular Mucosa) to split them!

paths.ifFinding: Afebrile / Subacute Blisters, Grouped Vesicles, or Acral Targets
paths.why: Non-fulminant presentation excludes TEN and SSSS—proceed to Gate 3 (Blister Roof Tension & Nikolsky).

steps.title: Gate 2 (Acute Sloughing): Inspect Oral, Conjunctival & Genital Mucosa
steps.ruleQuestion: Are hemorrhagic crusted oral/conjunctival mucosal erosions PRESENT or COMPLETELY SPARED?

paths.ifFinding: SEVERE Oral / Ocular / Genital Mucositis + Full-Thickness Necrosis Post-Drug
paths.why: CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell keratinocyte apoptosis destroys full-thickness epidermis AND mucosa (<10% BSA = SJS; >30% BSA = TEN)—EXCLUDING SSSS and Erythema Multiforme minor.

paths.ifFinding: Oral Mucosa COMPLETELY SPARED in Newborn / Young Child
paths.why: S. aureus exfoliative toxin A/B cleaves ONLY Desmoglein-1 in the superficial stratum granulosum (oral mucosa expresses Desmoglein-3, so mucosa stays 100% intact!)—EXCLUDING SJS/TEN and Pemphigus vulgaris!

steps.title: Gate 3 (Autoimmune Bullae): Test Blister Tension, Nikolsky Sign & Oral Ulcers
steps.ruleQuestion: Are bullae FLACCID/fragile with oral erosions (Nikolsky +), TENSE/intact sparing mouth (Nikolsky −), or pruritic extensor microvesicles?

paths.ifFinding: FLACCID Easily Ruptured Bullae + Painful Oral Erosions + Nikolsky (+)
paths.why: Intraepidermal acantholysis leaves thin roofs that rupture easily and hits Desmoglein-3 in oral mucosa—DECISIVELY EXCLUDING Bullous Pemphigoid!

paths.ifFinding: TENSE Intact Bullae in Elderly + Oral Mucosa SPARED + Nikolsky (−)
paths.why: Full intact epidermis forms the thick roof above a subepidermal hemidesmosomal split—EXCLUDING Pemphigus vulgaris.

paths.ifFinding: Intensely Pruritic Grouped Vesicles on Elbows/Knees OR Acral Target Rings
paths.why: Symmetric extensor elbows/knees = Dermatitis herpetiformis (Celiac!). Concentric targetoid plaques on palms/soles post-HSV or Mycoplasma = Erythema multiforme. Dermatomal/labial dewdrop on rose petal + Tzanck multinucleated giant cells = VZV/HSV.

steps.title: Gate 4: Lock Autoimmune Blistering Diagnosis with Direct Immunofluorescence (IF)
steps.ruleQuestion: What immunoglobulin class and pattern lights up on perilesional skin biopsy?

paths.ifFinding: Reticular "Fishnet / Chicken-Wire" Intercellular Epidermal IgG
paths.why: IgG coats Desmoglein 1 & 3 around every spinous keratinocyte ("row of tombstones" basal layer left behind).

paths.ifFinding: Smooth LINEAR IgG & C3 Along Dermoepidermal Basement Membrane
paths.why: IgG targets hemidesmosome BP180 / BP230 anchoring basal cells to lamina lucida + eosinophil infiltrate.

paths.ifFinding: GRANULAR IgA Clumps at Tips of Dermal Papillae
paths.why: Anti-epidermal transglutaminase IgA + neutrophil microabscesses—100% pathognomonic for Celiac disease (treat w/ strict gluten-free diet + dapsone!).

steps.title: Gate 5: Exclude Porphyria Cutanea Tarda in Dorsal Hand Blisters
steps.ruleQuestion: What if painless blisters + hypertrichosis appear strictly on sun-exposed DORSAL HANDS with tea-colored urine?

paths.ifFinding: Photosensitive Dorsal Hand Fragility + Hep C / Alcohol + Coral-Red Urine Fluorescence
paths.why: Locks Porphyria Cutanea Tarda (UROD uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase deficiency → elevated urine uroporphyrins; triggered by Hepatitis C, alcohol, estrogens, and HFE hemochromatosis; treat w/ phlebotomy!).

steps.title: Gate 1: Separate Metabolic Fasting Hypoglycemia vs. Progressive Lysosomal Storage
steps.ruleQuestion: Does the infant crash with acute fasting/feeding HYPOGLYCEMIA, or present at 3–12 months with developmental regression / coarse facies / normal glucose?

paths.ifFinding: Acute Fasting or Post-Feeding HYPOGLYCEMIA (Lethargy, Seizures, Vomiting)
paths.why: True hypoglycemia proves impaired gluconeogenesis, glycogenolysis, or ATP-trapping sugar-phosphate accumulation—IMMEDIATELY EXCLUDING Pompe disease (lysosomal glycogen, NORMAL blood glucose!) and all sphingolipidoses/MPS!

paths.ifFinding: NORMAL Blood Glucose + Hypotonia / Cardiomegaly / Regression / Organomegaly
paths.why: Normal fasting glucose excludes cytosolic G6Pase and β-oxidation defects and isolates lysosomal storage disorders—proceed to Gate 4.

steps.title: Gate 2 (Hypoglycemia): Check Serum/Urine Ketones & Dietary Sugar Trigger
steps.ruleQuestion: During hypoglycemia, are ketones ABSENT, or did symptoms begin right after breastmilk vs. fruit juice?

paths.ifFinding: HYPOKETOTIC Hypoglycemia After Overnight Fast / Viral Illness (↓↓ Ketones)
paths.why: Without β-oxidation, the liver cannot make ketone bodies OR acetyl-CoA to activate pyruvate carboxylase—confirm MCAD via ↑ C8–C10 acylcarnitines & dicarboxylic acids (vs. low free carnitine + muscle weakness in Systemic Carnitine deficiency).

paths.ifFinding: Triggered by Breastmilk (Day 3) vs. First Weaning to Fruit/Honey (6 Months) + Urine Reducing Sugars (+)
paths.why: Day 3 breastmilk/lactose + oil-drop cataracts + jaundice + E. coli neonatal sepsis = Classic Galactosemia (GALT). Age 6 mo weaning to sucrose/fruit juice = Hereditary Fructose Intolerance (Aldolase B)—EXCLUDING benign galactokinase & essential fructosuria (which NEVER cause hypoglycemia or liver failure!).

steps.title: Gate 3 (Ketotic Fasting Hypoglycemia + Massive Hepatomegaly): Check Blood Lactate
steps.ruleQuestion: In glycogen storage hepatomegaly with fasting hypoglycemia, are blood lactate and uric acid sky-high or NORMAL?

paths.ifFinding: SEVERE Lactic Acidosis + ↑↑ Uric Acid (Gout) + ↑↑ Triglycerides + Doll-Like Face
paths.why: Glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency blocks the final step of BOTH glycogenolysis AND gluconeogenesis (trapped G6P backs up into lactate & HMP purines)—EXCLUDING Cori!

paths.ifFinding: Milder Fasting Hypoglycemia + NORMAL Blood Lactate + Cytosolic Limit Dextrin + Muscle Weakness
paths.why: Debranching enzyme (α-1,6-glucosidase) deficiency leaves gluconeogenesis 100% INTACT, so blood lactate stays NORMAL!

steps.title: Gate 4 (Lysosomal, Normal Glucose): Check Cardiomegaly, Cherry-Red Macula & Hepatosplenomegaly
steps.ruleQuestion: Does the infant have massive cardiomegaly ("Pompe trashes the Pump"), or a macular cherry-red spot WITH vs. WITHOUT hepatosplenomegaly?

paths.ifFinding: Floppy Infant + MASSIVE Biventricular Cardiomegaly + Macroglossia + ↑ CK
paths.why: Lysosomal acid α-1,4-glucosidase (acid maltase) deficiency packs cardiac & skeletal muscle lysosomes with glycogen while sparing blood glucose.

paths.ifFinding: Macular Cherry-Red Spot + Hyperacusis Startle + NO Hepatosplenomegaly
paths.why: Normal liver/spleen size DECISIVELY EXCLUDES Niemann-Pick! Hexosaminidase A deficiency → GM2 ganglioside onion-skin lysosomes.

paths.ifFinding: Macular Cherry-Red Spot + YES Hepatosplenomegaly + Lipid Foam Cells
paths.why: Hepatosplenomegaly + cherry-red spot locks Sphingomyelinase deficiency (Niemann-Pick Type A) and EXCLUDES Tay-Sachs!

steps.title: Gate 5: Split Gaucher vs. Hurler vs. Hunter (Bone Crises & Corneal Clouding)
steps.ruleQuestion: In hepatosplenomegaly WITHOUT a cherry-red spot, check bone marrow smears and corneas:

paths.ifFinding: Hepatosplenomegaly + Pancytopenia + Avascular Femur Necrosis + Crumpled Tissue-Paper Macrophages
paths.why: Glucocerebrosidase (β-glucosidase) deficiency—#1 lysosomal storage disease; no corneal clouding or gargoyle facies.

paths.ifFinding: Coarse Gargoyle Facies + Dysostosis Multiplex → Split by Corneal Clouding!
paths.why: CORNEAL CLOUDING (+) = AR Hurler (α-L-iduronidase). CLEAR CORNEAS (no clouding — "Hunters see clearly to aim!") + aggressive X-linked boy = Hunter (iduronate-2-sulfatase)!

funnels.chiefComplaint: Fever, Headache, Meningitis & Focal CNS Infections
startingPool: Bacterial Meningitis (S. pneumo / N. meningitidis / GBS / Listeria)

steps.title: Gate 1: Check Focal Neurologic Deficits / Seizures & Head CT Mass Lesions BEFORE LP
steps.ruleQuestion: Does Head CT/MRI show discrete ring-enhancing mass lesion(s) or temporal lobe necrosis, OR diffuse meningeal inflammation?

paths.ifFinding: Ring-Enhancing Mass Lesion(s) on Brain MRI (Do NOT LP if Mass Shift!)
excludes: Bacterial Meningitis (S. pneumo / N. meningitidis / GBS / Listeria)
paths.why: Parenchymal ring-enhancing masses immediately separate focal space-occupying lesions from leptomeningitis—proceed to Gate 2 to split Toxoplasmosis vs. CNS Lymphoma vs. Abscess/Taenia!

paths.ifFinding: Meningismus (Neck Stiffness, Photophobia) Without Mass Shift → Proceed to CSF LP
keeps: Bacterial Meningitis (S. pneumo / N. meningitidis / GBS / Listeria)
paths.why: Safe to perform lumbar puncture—proceed to Gate 3 (CSF Cell Type & Glucose).

steps.title: Gate 2 (Brain Mass): Split HIV Toxoplasma vs. EBV Lymphoma vs. Pork Tapeworm vs. Bacterial Abscess
steps.ruleQuestion: In ring-enhancing brain lesions, check HIV CD4 count, lesion multiplicity, and pork/sinus/dental history:

paths.ifFinding: HIV CD4 <100 + MULTIPLE Basal Ganglia Ring Lesions → Responds to Sulfadiazine/Pyrimethamine
paths.why: Multiple subcortical/basal ganglia lesions shrinking within 2 weeks of pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine (+ leucovorin) confirm Toxoplasma gondii and EXCLUDE CNS lymphoma.

paths.ifFinding: HIV CD4 <50 + SOLITARY Periventricular Ring Lesion + EBV CSF PCR (+)
paths.why: Solitary periventricular/corpus callosum lesion failing Toxoplasma therapy with EBV DNA in CSF locks Primary CNS Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma!

paths.ifFinding: Immunocompetent Immigrant w/ Seizures + Calcified "Swiss-Cheese" Cysts OR Otitis/Dental Source
paths.why: Ingested Taenia solium EGGS (fecal-oral, NOT undercooked pork cysts, which cause intestinal tapeworm!) + eosinophilia = Neurocysticercosis (albendazole + steroids). Contiguous sinusitis/otitis/mastoiditis/endocarditis solitary abscess = Viridans strep + anaerobes.

steps.title: Gate 3 (Lumbar Puncture): Split CSF Predominant WBC (PMNs vs. Lymphocytes) & CSF Glucose
steps.ruleQuestion: Are neutrophils (>1,000 PMNs) dominating, or lymphocytes—and is CSF glucose LOW (<40 mg/dL) or NORMAL?

paths.ifFinding: NEUTROPHILIC Pleocytosis + ↓↓ CSF Glucose + ↑↑ Protein
keeps: Bacterial Meningitis (S. pneumo / N. meningitidis / GBS / Listeria)
paths.why: PMN dominance + glucose consumption confirms pyogenic Bacterial Meningitis and EXCLUDES viral, fungal, and TB meningitis!

paths.ifFinding: LYMPHOCYTIC Pleocytosis + NORMAL CSF Glucose
excludes: Bacterial Meningitis (S. pneumo / N. meningitidis / GBS / Listeria)
paths.why: Normal CSF glucose DECISIVELY EXCLUDES bacterial, fungal, and tuberculous meningitis! Self-limiting summer/fall headache = Coxsackie/Echovirus; temporal lobe hemorrhage + bizarre behavior/olfactory hallucinations + CSF RBCs = HSV-1 Encephalitis (IV acyclovir immediately!).

paths.ifFinding: LYMPHOCYTIC Pleocytosis + LOW CSF Glucose + ↑↑ Opening Pressure
excludes: Bacterial Meningitis (S. pneumo / N. meningitidis / GBS / Listeria)
paths.why: Lymphocytes + LOW glucose isolates Fungal vs. Tuberculous meningitis—proceed to Gate 5 to split them!

steps.title: Gate 4 (Bacterial PMN CSF): Lock Exact Bacterium by Patient Age & Gram Morphology
steps.ruleQuestion: What is the patient's age and Gram stain shape?

paths.ifFinding: Neonate (<1 Month): GBS · E. coli K1 · Listeria (Tumbling Gram + Rod)
keeps: Bacterial Meningitis (S. pneumo / N. meningitidis / GBS / Listeria)
paths.why: Always add AMPICILLIN in neonates (<1 mo), elderly (>50 yo), and immunocompromised/pregnant patients to cover Listeria monocytogenes (cephalosporins alone FAIL against Listeria!). Teen w/ petechial purpura + Gram(−) diplococci = N. meningitidis; Adult #1 = Gram(+) lancet diplococci S. pneumoniae.

steps.title: Gate 5 (Lymphocytic + Low Glucose): Split Cryptococcus vs. TB Meningitis
steps.ruleQuestion: Check HIV CD4 count, Cryptococcal Antigen / India Ink, and Basal Cistern Enhancement:

paths.ifFinding: HIV CD4 <100 + CrAg Latex Agglutination (+) + India Ink Halo / Mucicarmine (+)
paths.why: Thick polysaccharide capsule yeast; induction = Amphotericin B + Flucytosine, followed by Fluconazole maintenance.

paths.ifFinding: Basilar Meningeal Enhancement + CN VI Palsy + Endemic Exposure / Acid-Fast (+)
paths.why: Exudate at base of brain entraps Cranial Nerves (especially CN III/VI) + hydrocephalus + SIADH; treat w/ RIPE + dexamethasone.

steps.title: Gate 1: Check Infant Age at Onset (<6 Months vs. >6 Months) & Pathogen Class
steps.ruleQuestion: Did severe viral/fungal/Thrush infections start right after birth (<6 mo), or did encapsulated bacterial infections begin AFTER 6 months (when maternal IgG waned)?

paths.ifFinding: Onset AFTER 6 Months · Encapsulated Sinopulmonary Bacteria & Giardia
paths.why: Transplacental maternal IgG protected the infant for the first 6 months—proving a B-Cell / Humoral Antibody defect and EXCLUDING SCID, DiGeorge & LAD-1!

paths.ifFinding: Onset BEFORE 6 Months · Candida Thrush, Chronic Viral Diarrhea & Pneumocystis
paths.why: Intracellular viral, fungal & opportunistic pathogens in early infancy prove a T-Cell / Combined defect—pure B-cell and complement defects are EXCLUDED.

paths.ifFinding: Skin/Organ Abscesses (No Pus vs. Catalase+) OR Recurrent Neisseria Only
paths.why: Isolates Innate Phagocyte or Complement MAC defects—proceed to Gate 4.

steps.title: Gate 2 (Humoral): Measure CD19+ B-Cell Count & Serum IgG / IgA / IgM
steps.ruleQuestion: Are peripheral CD19+ B cells ABSENT, or are B cells NORMAL in number with specific immunoglobulin gaps?

paths.ifFinding: ABSENT CD19+ B Cells + Absent Tonsils/Lymph Nodes + Zero IgG/IgA/IgM in a Boy
paths.why: BTK tyrosine kinase mutation arrests pre-B → mature B differentiation in bone marrow—EXCLUDING CVID, IgA def., and Hyper-IgM (all of which have NORMAL CD19+ B-cell counts!).

paths.ifFinding: Normal CD19+ B Cells + SKY-HIGH IgM + Absent IgG/IgA/IgE (+ Pneumocystis!)
paths.why: Defective CD40L on helper T cells prevents class-switching AND macrophage activation—uniquely adding opportunistic Pneumocystis/Cryptosporidium to a humoral picture!

paths.ifFinding: Normal CD19+ B Cells + Low All Igs in Teen/20s (CVID) vs. Isolated Low IgA
paths.why: Isolated ↓ IgA (normal IgG/IgM) = Selective IgA Deficiency (watch for anaphylaxis to blood transfusion!). Teen/young adult w/ ↓ IgG, ↓ IgA, ↓ IgM + autoimmune cytopenias/lymphoma risk = CVID (defective plasma cell differentiation).

steps.title: Gate 3 (T-Cell / Combined): Check Serum Ca²⁺, Thymic Shadow, B-Cell Function & Platelets
steps.ruleQuestion: Is hypocalcemic tetany + conotruncal heart defect present, total lymphopenia, or microthrombocytopenia + eczema?

paths.ifFinding: Hypocalcemic Tetany + Absent Thymic Shadow + Truncus/TOF (Normal B Cells)
paths.why: Failed 3rd & 4th pharyngeal pouch development eliminates thymus (↓ CD3+ T cells) AND parathyroids (↓ PTH, ↓↓ Ca²⁺)—EXCLUDING SCID (which has normal calcium + nonfunctional B cells!).

paths.ifFinding: Absent Thymic Shadow + Absent TRECs on Newborn Screen + Absent T AND B Function
paths.why: X-linked IL-2Rγ common gamma chain (#1) or AR Adenosine Deaminase deficiency (toxic dATP kills all lymphocytes)—medical emergency requiring stem cell transplant (avoid all live vaccines!).

paths.ifFinding: WATER Triad: Thrombocytopenia (Small Platelets) + Eczema + ↑ IgE/IgA, ↓ IgM
paths.why: X-linked WASp actin cytoskeleton reorganization defect impairs T-cell immunological synapse & megakaryocyte platelet shedding.

steps.title: Gate 4 (Innate): Split Delayed Umbilical Cord vs. Catalase+ DHR Test vs. Neisseria
steps.ruleQuestion: Check umbilical cord separation history, neutrophil count/pus, and Dihydrorhodamine (DHR) flow cytometry:

paths.ifFinding: Delayed Umbilical Cord Separation (>30 Days) + Marked Neutrophilia + ZERO Pus
paths.why: Absent CD18 (β2-integrin LFA-1) traps neutrophils inside blood vessels so they cannot migrate into tissues to form pus or digest the umbilical stump!

paths.ifFinding: ABNORMAL DHR (No Green Fluorescence) / Negative NBT + Catalase (+) Infections
paths.why: NADPH oxidase deficiency: neutrophils migrate normally (pus/granulomas form!) but cannot generate superoxide against catalase+ organisms (S. aureus, Pseudomonas, Serratia, Nocardia, Aspergillus). Note: MPO deficiency has abnormal MPO but intact H₂O₂ → largely asymptomatic except Candida in diabetics!

steps.title: Gate 5: Confirm Isolated Recurrent Neisseria Meningitidis / Gonorrhoeae
steps.ruleQuestion: What if a teen/young adult has NORMAL B, T, and phagocyte counts with recurrent Neisseria bacteremia?

paths.ifFinding: Normal Immunoglobulins + Undetectable CH50 + Recurrent Neisseria Only
paths.why: Inability to assemble Membrane Attack Complex (MAC C5b–C9) selectively impairs lysis of thin-walled Gram-negative Neisseria diplococci.

funnels.chiefComplaint: Unknown Biopsy Cell Death, Granuloma or Extracellular Deposit

steps.title: Gate 1: Is Surrounding Acute Inflammation Present (Membrane Rupture) or Absent?
steps.ruleQuestion: Did cell membranes stay intact with shrunk eosinophilic single cells, or burst with contiguous tissue inflammation?

paths.ifFinding: Single-Cell Shrinkage + Intact Membrane Blebs + ZERO Surrounding Inflammation
paths.why: ATP-dependent caspase cleavage (180-bp DNA ladder; Councilman body in viral hepatitis, embryogenesis, CD8+ killing) keeps intracellular DAMPs sealed inside apoptotic bodies—EXCLUDING all forms of necrosis!

paths.ifFinding: Confluent Cell Death + Membrane Rupture + Inflammatory Infiltrate OR Acellular Deposit
paths.why: Excludes apoptosis—proceed to Gate 2 (Preserved Outlines vs. Pus/Brain Cavity vs. Vessel Wall vs. Granuloma).

steps.title: Gate 2: Inspect Tissue Architecture (Ghost Outlines vs. Viscous Cavity vs. Chalky Fat)
steps.ruleQuestion: Are cellular outlines preserved like tombstones, dissolved into liquid, or calcified in adipose tissue?

paths.ifFinding: Preserved Anucleate Eosinophilic "Ghost" Cell Outlines (Wedge Infarct)
paths.why: Ischemic acidosis denatures proteolytic enzymes in Heart, Kidney & Spleen—EXCLUDING CNS ischemia!

paths.ifFinding: Complete Enzymatic Digestion into Fluid/Cystic Cavity (Brain Infarct or Abscess)
paths.why: CNS microglial hydrolytic enzymes (brain stroke → astrocyte glial scar surrounding cystic cavity) or neutrophil elastases (bacterial abscess) liquefy architecture completely.

paths.ifFinding: Chalky-White Saponified Adipocyte Outlines + Basophilic Ca²⁺ Soap
paths.why: Free fatty acids released by acute pancreatitis lipase or breast trauma bind Ca²⁺ via saponification (causes hypocalcemia in severe pancreatitis!).

steps.title: Gate 3 (Pink Amorphous Material): Split Fibrinoid Vessel Necrosis vs. Extracellular Amyloid
steps.ruleQuestion: When H&E shows bright pink amorphous material, is it inside inflamed arterial walls or extracellular stroma?

paths.ifFinding: Bright Smudgy Pink Inside Arteriolar Walls + Neutrophils (Malignant HTN / PAN)
paths.why: Immune complexes + leaked plasma fibrin within vessel media (Polyarteritis nodosa, preeclampsia, malignant hypertension "onion-skinning")—Congo red NEGATIVE!

paths.ifFinding: Acellular Waxy Pink Extracellular Matrix → Apple-Green Birefringence on Congo Red
paths.why: β-pleated sheet fibrils (AL κ/λ light chains in myeloma; AA serum amyloid A in chronic inflammation; ATTR in senile/familial cardiomyopathy; β₂-microglobulin in dialysis).

steps.title: Gate 4 (Epithelioid Histiocytes + Langhans Giant Cells): Check Central Caseation
steps.ruleQuestion: Does the Th1 IFN-γ macrophage granuloma have a necrotic cheese-like center or remain intact (noncaseating)?

paths.ifFinding: CASEATING Central Acellular Necrosis
paths.why: Caseous necrosis IMMEDIATELY EXCLUDES Sarcoidosis, Crohn disease & Berylliosis—stain immediately with Ziehl-Neelsen (acid-fast M. tuberculosis) and GMS silver stain (Histoplasma/Coccidioides)!

paths.ifFinding: NONCASEATING Intact Epithelioid Granuloma (Zero Central Necrosis)
paths.why: Rule out infectious fungi/AFB first, then split noncaseating causes: Bilateral hilar nodes + ↑ ACE/Ca²⁺ = Sarcoidosis; Transmural ileocolitis = Crohn; Aerospace dust = Berylliosis; Catalase+ child = CGD; Foreign body.

steps.title: Gate 5: Final Dystrophic vs. Metastatic Tissue Calcification Check
steps.ruleQuestion: If basophilic calcium granules appear on biopsy, check the patient's SERUM Ca²⁺:

paths.ifFinding: NORMAL Serum Ca²⁺ (Dystrophic) vs. HIGH Serum Ca²⁺/PO₄³⁻ (Metastatic)
paths.why: Calcification in damaged/necrotic tissue (Ghon complex, fat necrosis, psammoma bodies, calcific aortic valve) has NORMAL serum Ca²⁺; calcium depositing in normal lung/kidney/stomach interstitium requires systemic hypercalcemia/ESRD!

startingPool: MDD or Bipolar w/ Psychotic Features

steps.title: Gate 1: Exclude Delirium, Substance Intoxication/Withdrawal & Medical Causes First
steps.ruleQuestion: Is consciousness/attention waxing and waning acutely, or are vitals/labs/tox screen abnormal?

paths.ifFinding: Fluctuating Attention/Awareness ("Sundowning") OR Abnormal Vitals/Pupils/Tox
paths.why: Primary psychiatric disorders ALWAYS have a clear sensorium and normal vital signs! Fluctuating attention in hospitalized elderly (infection/anticholinergics) = Delirium; rotary nystagmus = PCP; visual hallucinations in parkinsonism = Lewy body dementia; tactile formication + mydriasis = Stimulants/Alcohol DT.

paths.ifFinding: Alert, Oriented Sensorium + Normal Vitals & Negative Medical/Tox Screen
keeps: MDD or Bipolar w/ Psychotic Features
paths.why: Establishes primary psychiatric etiology—proceed immediately to Gate 2 (Hallucinations/Disorganization vs. Isolated Delusion).

steps.title: Gate 2: Check for Hallucinations, Disorganized Speech & Daily Functioning
steps.ruleQuestion: Does the patient have ONLY a fixed delusion for ≥1 month while working/functioning normally?

paths.ifFinding: Fixed Delusion(s) ≥1 Month + ZERO Hallucinations + INTACT Daily Work/Social Function
paths.why: Erotomanic, jealous, persecutory, or somatic delusions with preserved daily functioning and no prominent hallucinations/negative symptoms locks Delusional Disorder and EXCLUDES Schizophrenia!

paths.ifFinding: Hallucinations, Disorganized Speech/Behavior, or Negative Symptoms Present
keeps: MDD or Bipolar w/ Psychotic Features
paths.why: True psychotic syndrome—proceed to Gate 3 (Mood Episode Concurrence Split!).

steps.title: Gate 3: Split Pure Psychosis vs. Schizoaffective vs. Mood Disorder w/ Psychotic Features
steps.ruleQuestion: Did hallucinations/delusions EVER persist for ≥2 weeks in the COMPLETE ABSENCE of mania or major depression?

paths.ifFinding: Psychosis Occurs EXCLUSIVELY During Manic or Major Depressive Episodes
keeps: MDD or Bipolar w/ Psychotic Features
paths.why: When mood resolves, psychosis resolves too—this 100% EXCLUDES Schizoaffective disorder and Schizophrenia!
paths.topicTitle: Major depressive disorder (MDD) with psychotic features

paths.ifFinding: Major Mood Episodes + ≥2 Weeks of Isolated Psychosis WITHOUT Any Mood Symptoms
excludes: MDD or Bipolar w/ Psychotic Features
paths.why: The ≥2-week mood-free psychosis window is the exact DSM board splitter that proves Schizoaffective Disorder over Mood w/ Psychotic Features!

paths.ifFinding: Pure Psychosis Without Prominent Mania or Major Depression
excludes: MDD or Bipolar w/ Psychotic Features
paths.why: Proceed to Gate 4 (Exact Calendar Stopwatch) for the final split.

steps.title: Gate 4: Apply the Exact 1-Month and 6-Month Stopwatch
steps.ruleQuestion: Counting prodromal + active + residual symptoms, how long has the episode lasted?

paths.ifFinding: 1 Day to < 1 Month (Full Return to Baseline)
paths.why: <30 days locks Brief Psychotic Disorder (often triggered by acute stressor or postpartum; note postpartum psychosis carries infanticide risk → emergency hospitalization!).

paths.ifFinding: 1 Month to < 6 Months
paths.why: 1–6 months locks Schizophreniform Disorder—cannot diagnose Schizophrenia until the 6-month mark is crossed!

paths.ifFinding: ≥ 6 Months Total (Including ≥1 Month Active-Phase Symptoms)
paths.why: Locks Schizophrenia (mesolimbic D2 hyperactivity = positive symptoms; mesocortical D2 hypoactivity = negative flat affect/avolition; enlarged cerebral ventricles & dendritic spine loss).

steps.title: Gate 5: Treatment-Resistant & Adverse-Effect Exclusion Check
steps.ruleQuestion: What if ≥2 antipsychotics fail, or fever + rigidity develops on treatment?

paths.ifFinding: Refractory Schizophrenia / Suicidality → Clozapine (Monitor ANC for Agranulocytosis!)
paths.why: If high fever + lead-pipe rigidity + ↑↑ CK develops after starting D2 antagonist → immediately STOP antipsychotic and give Dantrolene (Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome!).

funnels.chiefComplaint: Identifying Study Design, Effect Measure, Statistical Test & Bias

steps.title: Gate 1: Did Investigators Assign an Intervention or Merely Observe?
steps.ruleQuestion: Did researchers randomize/assign treatment, or observe naturally occurring exposures/outcomes?

paths.ifFinding: Investigators Randomly Assigned Treatment vs. Placebo/Standard of Care
paths.why: Randomization balances BOTH known and unknown confounders at baseline; calculate Absolute Risk Reduction `ARR = CER − EER` and `NNT = 1 / ARR`.

paths.ifFinding: No Intervention Assigned (Observational)
paths.why: Proceed immediately to Gate 2 (Timeline & Grouping Axis) to separate the 3 observational designs.

steps.title: Gate 2 (Observational): How Were Subjects Enrolled (Snapshot vs. Outcome vs. Exposure)?
steps.ruleQuestion: Were exposure & disease measured simultaneously, grouped by Disease (Cases vs. Controls), or grouped by Exposure and followed over time?

paths.ifFinding: Exposure & Outcome Measured at ONE Single Point in Time
paths.why: Measures Disease PREVALENCE; CANNOT establish temporal causality (whether exposure preceded disease).

paths.ifFinding: Grouped by OUTCOME (Patients WITH Rare Disease vs. Matched Controls) → Look Back
paths.why: MUST use Odds Ratio `OR = (a·d)/(b·c)` and EXCLUDES Relative Risk & Incidence (because researchers fixed the case:control ratio artificially!; vulnerable to Recall Bias).

paths.ifFinding: Grouped by EXPOSURE (Exposed vs. Unexposed Disease-Free) → Followed Forward (or via Historical Records)
paths.why: Directly measures INCIDENCE in exposed vs. unexposed → Relative Risk `RR = [a/(a+b)] ÷ [c/(c+d)]` and Attributable Risk.

steps.title: Gate 3 (Spurious Association Check): Apply Stratification to Split Confounding vs. Effect Modification
steps.ruleQuestion: When you stratify the study into Subgroups of Factor Z (e.g., Smokers vs. Non-Smokers), what happens to the OR/RR?

paths.ifFinding: Association DISAPPEARS (Stratum ORs Both Drop to ~1.0 and Equal Each Other)
paths.why: Proves Factor Z was a CONFOUNDER (connected to both exposure and outcome, creating a fake crude association—eliminate via matching, restriction, randomization, or multivariable regression!).

paths.ifFinding: Stratum ORs DIFFER Significantly From Each Other (e.g., OR = 8.0 in Group A vs. OR = 1.1 in Group B)
paths.why: Proves EFFECT MODIFICATION (true biological synergy/interaction, e.g., OCPs × Factor V Leiden, or Asbestos × Smoking)—report strata separately, DO NOT "adjust away"!

steps.title: Gate 4 (Screening Survival Trap): Exclude Lead-Time vs. Length-Time Bias
steps.ruleQuestion: Why did a new cancer screening test appear to improve "5-year survival" without reducing overall age-adjusted mortality?

paths.ifFinding: Earlier Diagnosis Starts Survival Timer Sooner Without Delaying Age of Death
paths.why: Locks LEAD-TIME Bias! (Whereas if screening catches slow-growing indolent tumors while missing aggressive fast-killing tumors between annual screens → LENGTH-TIME Bias!).

steps.title: Gate 5: Select the Right Hypothesis Test & Check Confidence Interval Null Exclusion
steps.ruleQuestion: Are the outcome and predictor Continuous Means or Categorical Proportions, and does the 95% CI exclude the null?

paths.ifFinding: Means: 2 Groups = t-Test · ≥3 Groups = ANOVA | Proportions (%): Chi-Square (χ²)
paths.why: Final significance rule: If a 95% CI for RR/OR includes `1.0` (e.g. `0.85–1.40`) or a 95% CI for mean difference/ARR includes `0` (e.g. `−1.2 to +3.4`), IMMEDIATELY EXCLUDE statistical significance (`p > 0.05`)!

funnels.chiefComplaint: Unknown Acute Drug Overdose / Autonomic Toxidrome

steps.title: Gate 1: Triage Vital Signs (Depressed HR/RR/Temp vs. Hyperthermic/Tachycardic)
steps.ruleQuestion: Is the patient "slow, cool, or apneic" (CNS/cholinergic depression) OR "hot, fast, and agitated" (hypermetabolic/autonomic storm)?

paths.ifFinding: DEPRESSED Respiration / Bradycardia / Hypothermia ("Cholinergic or Sedated")
paths.why: Slow RR or bradycardia IMMEDIATELY EXCLUDES anticholinergic, sympathomimetic, serotonin, and NMS storms!

paths.ifFinding: HYPERTHERMIA + TACHYCARDIA + Agitation / Hypertension
paths.why: Excludes opioids and sedative-hypnotics—proceed to Gate 3 (Sweat & Bowel Sounds) and Gate 4 (Clonus vs. Rigidity) to split the 4 hot toxidromes!

steps.title: Gate 2 (Depressed Vitals): Split Opioid vs. Cholinergic vs. Benzo Using Pupils & Secretions
steps.ruleQuestion: Are pupils pinpoint (2 mm) with dry airway vs. drowning in secretions, or mid-position?

paths.ifFinding: Pinpoint Miosis + Respiratory Rate <8/min + QUIET Lungs (No Bronchorrhea)
paths.why: Pure μ-receptor medullary respiratory depression + Edinger-Westphal miosis—antidote = IV/IN Naloxone!

paths.ifFinding: Pinpoint Miosis + PROFUSE Salivation, Bronchorrhea, Diarrhea, Fasciculations (DUMBBELSS)
paths.why: Excess ACh at M3 glands/bronchi + nicotinic NMJ fasciculations locks AChE inhibition—give Atropine FIRST + Pralidoxime (2-PAM)!

paths.ifFinding: Slurred Speech + Ataxia + NORMAL Pupils + Minimal Respiratory Drop (Unless Mixed w/ Alcohol!)
paths.why: GABA-A Cl⁻ channel potentiation (benzodiazepine ↑ frequency; barbiturate ↑ duration → severe respiratory arrest; avoid flumazenil if chronic benzo user or co-ingested TCA → precipitates seizures!).

steps.title: Gate 3 (Hot + Mydriatic + Tachycardic): Palpate Axillary Sweat & Auscultate Bowel Sounds
steps.ruleQuestion: Both Anticholinergics and Sympathomimetics dilate pupils and race the heart—is the skin BONE-DRY or DRENCHED IN SWEAT?

paths.ifFinding: BONE-DRY Flushed Skin + ABSENT Bowel Sounds + Urinary Retention + Delirium
paths.why: Eccrine sweat glands use sympathetic M3 ACh receptors—bone-dry axillae + silent gut DECISIVELY EXCLUDE sympathomimetics and serotonin syndrome! Check ECG QRS width (>100 ms in TCA overdose → give IV NaHCO₃!; pure antimuscarinic → physostigmine).

paths.ifFinding: DIAPHORETIC Sweaty Skin + Normal/Hyperactive Bowel Sounds
paths.why: Sweating immediately EXCLUDES anticholinergic poisoning—proceed to Gate 4 (Lower Extremity Tone & Reflexes).

steps.title: Gate 4 (Diaphoretic + Hyperthermic): Test Ankle Clonus, Reflexes & Rigidity
steps.ruleQuestion: Are lower extremities HYPERREFLEXIC with clonus, RIGID like a lead pipe, or normal?

paths.ifFinding: Normal Tone & Reflexes + Severe Hypertension / Chest Pain / Pupillary Dilation
paths.why: Treat agitation/HTN with Benzodiazepines (NEVER give pure β-blockers like propranolol in cocaine toxicity → unopposed α₁ coronary/systemic vasoconstriction!).

paths.ifFinding: HYPERREFLEXIA + Inducible Ankle CLONUS + Diarrhea (SSRI + MAOI/Tramadol/Linezolid)
paths.why: Clonus + hyperreflexia + hyperactive GI motility locks Serotonin Syndrome and EXCLUDES NMS—antidote = Cyproheptadine (5-HT2 antagonist).

paths.ifFinding: LEAD-PIPE Generalized Rigidity + Hyporeflexia + ↑↑↑ CK (On Haloperidol / Antipsychotic)
paths.why: Central D2 blockade causes severe muscular rigidity & rhabdomyolysis without clonus—antidote = Dantrolene (RYR1 blocker) or Bromocriptine (D2 agonist).

steps.title: Gate 5: Check Acid-Base, RUQ Liver & GI Radiopaque Pills (Metabolic Poisons)
steps.ruleQuestion: If autonomic signs are absent, check ABG, AST/ALT, venous O₂, and abdominal X-ray:

paths.ifFinding: Tinnitus + Mixed Resp Alkalosis/AG Acidosis (Salicylate) · RUQ NAPQI (APAP) · Smoke CN⁻ · Radiopaque Pills (Iron)
paths.why: Salicylate → IV NaHCO₃ urinary alkalinization; Acetaminophen → N-acetylcysteine; House-fire Cyanide (bitter almonds, bright red venous blood, lactic acidosis) → Hydroxocobalamin; Child swallowing prenatal vitamins + hematemesis + radiopaque gastric pills → Iron toxicity (Deferoxamine!).
